title: From report to deck

steps.say: Same tool, new format: format: revealjs makes a slide deck. The header's title and subtitle become the title slide.
Each ## heading starts a slide. The setup chunk works as in the report: group_by() and summarise() give each region's change, and inline R counts them.
A chunk on a slide puts its chart on the slide. Unlike a report, a deck hides code unless you ask for it.
A single # starts a section with its own title slide. The ## slides after it stack under it, and the arrow keys still walk through them in order.

---
title: "Unemployment in the regions"
subtitle: "Quarterly briefing · synthetic data"
format: revealjs
---

```{r}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
rates <- read_csv("unemployment.csv")
kingdom <- rates |> filter(region == "Kingdom")
jazan <- rates |> filter(region == "Jazan")
change <- rates |>
  filter(region != "Kingdom") |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarise(change = last(rate) - first(rate))
up <- change |> filter(change > 0) |> pull(region)
```

## Unemployment is falling

- Down in `r sum(change$change < 0)` of `r nrow(change)` regions since 2022
- It rose only in `r up`

## The national trend
